subject: Service update — transient throughput throttling (hosted inference)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@crescent.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Sep 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Service update — transient throughput throttling (hosted inference)

Hi Lina,

I wanted to reach out right away to let you know we detected elevated request queueing and reduced throughput for some hosted inference requests in the us-west region starting ~07:55 PDT. Our telemetry shows increased p95/p99 processing time for synchronous generation endpoints for sequences longer than ~1k tokens. We believe this impacted a subset of customer traffic — our monitoring flagged CrescentAI routed traffic during the window.

What we're doing now:
- Routes: diverting traffic away from the affected GPU pool to a healthy pool with compatible model variants (rolling).
- Prefix caching: invalidating a small set of stale KV cache entries that appear correlated with the slowdown.
- Autoscale: increasing dedicated burst capacity for short-term headroom.

Estimated impact window: we observed the first signs at 07:55 PDT and began mitigations at 08:05 PDT. We expect throughput to normalize within 1-2 hours as routing and cache stabilization complete; we will send a follow-up when we confirm full recovery.

Immediate ask from you: can you confirm whether CrescentAI saw increased 429/503 responses or prolonged token-level latencies during the 07:55–08:15 PDT window? Any sample request ids will help with matching logs.

I've attached a brief ops snapshot (ops_snapshot.png) and an incident timeline CSV; we'll share a postmortem link once internal triage completes. Ben and Sean are on the incident channel and copied here.

Sorry for the disruption — we know these windows matter. I will keep you updated every time we hit a new milestone (mitigation started, stabilized, fully recovered).

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): ops_snapshot.png (PNG), incident_timeline.csv (CSV)

We did see user-facing slowdowns and a handful of 503s between ~07:58–08:12 PDT. Our logs include request ids for four affected calls: cres-req-8921, cres-req-8927, cres-req-8930, cres-req-8934. Happy to share full traces if useful.

Two asks from our side: 1) will there be any token-level reruns that could affect billing (we want to understand if we should expect anomalous usage spikes), and 2) are you able to provide an ETA for a formal postmortem + whether CrescentAI will be eligible for service credits per the SLA for this window?

Lina

Mina / Sean — quick internal note:

- Root cause signal (preliminary): KV cache staleness + a rare bulk-prefetch fanout that amplified I/O to a small set of GPUs. When combined with an unusual tokenization distribution for long sequences it pushed the pool into high scheduling latency.
- Mitigations applied: routing diversion completed at 08:08 PDT; manual cache invalidation at 08:10 PDT; autoscale added +20% burst capacity at 08:12 PDT.
- Current status: backend p95 has dropped back near baseline but p99 tails are still elevated for long sequences — we're watching.

Action items:
1) Mina — please send the external status update (I drafted a short statuspage blurb below).
2) Sean — continue capture of slow traces and attach to RED-8721.
3) Ops — collect timeline CSV and attach snapshots (already in progress).

Draft statuspage blurb (feel free to shorten):
"Starting 07:55 PDT, a subset of hosted inference requests experienced degraded throughput resulting in increased latency and some 503 responses for customers routed to one GPU pool in us-west. We routed traffic to healthy pools and invalidated impacted cache entries; full recovery observed by 09:10 PDT. Engineering is investigating root cause and will publish a post-incident report"

If you want, I can open a formal SLA credit request template for Crescent; Mina, let me know and I'll start it.

Ben
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@crescent.ai>, Crescent Support <support@crescent.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 Sep 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — 2028-09-29 us-west throughput event

Hi Lina and team,

Thank you for your patience while we completed triage. This is our post-incident summary and the next steps we are taking. If you'd prefer a short call, we can schedule one — otherwise this note and the linked postmortem cover the details.

Summary
- Incident start: 07:55 PDT (2028-09-29) — anomalous queueing observed for long-sequence hosted inference requests in us-west.
- Mitigation actions: traffic diversion to a healthy GPU pool (08:08 PDT), manual KV cache invalidation (08:10 PDT), autoscale burst (08:12 PDT).
- Recovery: backend throughput and p95 returned to baseline by 09:10 PDT. p99 tails for very long sequences normalized by ~12:00 PDT after additional kernel scheduling fixes.

Root cause (short): a combination of an edge-case prefetch fanout that triggered heavy I/O against a limited GPU pool and a cache-staleness pathway that increased misrouted work. The combination produced scheduling latency amplifications for long sequences. Engineering has recorded a reproduction test and the fix path includes an additional guardrail in prefetch logic and a scheduled cache-rotation job.

Impact to CrescentAI
- We observed the 503/latency symptoms you reported for the request ids you supplied (cres-req-8921, cres-req-8927, cres-req-8930, cres-req-8934) and matched them to traces in RED-8721.
- Token-level billing: we are auditing the affected requests for any duplicated token charges or replays. Preliminary assessment: there were a small number of retried calls at the edge; we will follow up with a billing reconciliation and credit recommendation by end of next week.

Attachments and links
- Attached: incident_timeline.csv (detailed timeline), ops_snapshot.png (cluster metrics), postmortem_draft.docx (internal draft).
- Postmortem (public draft): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2B3cPostmortemDraft
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-8721
- Status page entry: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-09-29-aurora-queueing

Next steps
- Engineering will ship a prefetch guard and a cache-rotation scheduler in the next deploy (planned 2028-10-05).
- We'll perform a billing audit for impacted calls and propose a credit per our SLA; Ben will start the credit request.
- We'll share a final public postmortem once internal and legal reviews are complete (target: 2028-10-07).

If you have any follow-up questions or want to review traces in a joint session, say the word and we'll arrange time.

Again, very sorry for the impact — we're committed to preventing recurrence.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
